clue.text: Run off with pins and needles for a short time

parts.note: to run off is to flee
pins and needles is a tingly feeling in a limb

explanation.surface: Someone bolting while their legs prickle with pins and needles, but only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting lasts only a moment, so fleetingly means briefly.

clue.text: Carbon will puncture spare tyre in particular

indicators.note: a thing that punctures goes right through, so carbon sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a spare tyre is jocular slang for a roll of fat round the waist
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Carbon fibre or a nail puncturing the spare tyre of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'particular' is the noun, as in 'the particulars of the case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single detail or item of information, much like a datum or point.

clue.text: Round headland, see running fugitive

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the shuffled letters go either side of the headland
running water flows and changes, here the letters of see are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A sailor told to round the headland and see a fugitive running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges see to ESE; 'Round' says those letters go either side of the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is a person who has got away from custody, an escaped runaway.

clue.text: First piece of opera singer told he must perform? Could be

definitions.text: First piece of opera singer told he must perform? Could be

indicators.note: to perform is to act out, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement
the first piece of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A singer told to perform the opening of an opera, which might be a Gilbert and Sullivan piece.
explanation.walkthrough: O (first of opera) plus SINGER, TOLD and HE are rearranged; 'must perform' is the anagram signal. The whole clue also hints at the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan about two Venetian boatmen, so a singer performing could well be in it.

clue.text: Tucking into bananas endlessly, there's nothing for Frenchman to make healthy bit of food

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the French word sits within the other piece
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is nutty
rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tucking into bananas finds nothing else to eat that is healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final Y; 'Tucking into' places the French word for nothing inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance in food that nourishes the body, such as a vitamin or protein.

clue.text: Spike Milligan ultimately trapped by 'Spike'

indicators.note: something trapped by another is held inside it

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: The comedian Spike Milligan finally caught by someone called Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan was a famous British comic writer; his name is a distraction here.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike and the other word are both pointed weapons or shafts; to spike is to pierce.

clue.text: Work a large stone

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Moving a big stone as a labour.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a milky iridescent gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: Church leader needs pollsters to overturn argument

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means flipped, so the pollsters' letters run backwards

parts.note: NOP, National Opinion Polls, is a British polling organisation
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A church leader who needs the pollsters to reverse an argument against him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is called the Supreme Pontiff, head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Try sailing at sea — it's a pain in the neck

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds trying to go sailing in rough weather a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a pain in the neck' means a nuisance, but here it is taken literally as a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the voice box in the throat, literally a pain in the neck.

clue.text: Constant pain in store

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A shopworker suffering persistent pain at the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden stock or hoard of supplies.

clue.text: In row, no writer offers penetrating article for the household

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the inner pieces sit inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An argument where a writer offers no penetrating comment on household matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In row' first reads as 'in a quarrel', but row is a tier of seats; 'penetrating' sends the writer inside. 'In' and 'offers' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kitchen gadget for opening cans, an everyday domestic utensil.

clue.text: Be reluctant to co-operate in obscure piece of drama

parts.note: a play is a piece of drama
something obscure is hard to get, that is hard to grasp

explanation.surface: An actor unwilling to help with a puzzling bit of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes feigning disinterest or being coy and unhelpful to provoke pursuit.

clue.text: Growth for helping to secure our time on earth

indicators.note: to secure is to hold safely within, so the lifetime sits inside

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a ration is a helping or allotted portion
a life is one's time on earth

explanation.surface: Something that grows by helping people secure their time on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for helping' together forms the container; 'to secure' says our time on earth sits between its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is rapid increase or spread, a kind of growth in number.

clue.text: Treat facts carelessly — it's politicians' talent

indicators.note: done carelessly means sloppily arranged, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dig at politicians whose real skill is treating facts loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the skill of managing public affairs and governing a nation.

clue.text: Telegraph leader's cutting becoming very popular

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: rending is tearing, cutting apart

explanation.surface: A Telegraph leading article whose cutting remarks are going viral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' also suggests a newspaper editorial, here it just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trending describes a topic currently gaining wide attention, especially online.

clue.text: Look close, I will pick up fellow

indicators.note: picking up something means taking it in, so the fellow sits inside

parts.note: to shut is to close

explanation.surface: Someone saying they will have a close look and collect a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Shufti is British slang, from Arabic, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A shufti is a quick glance or peek at something, an informal British word.

clue.text: Path that can take one to Broadway?

definitions.text: Path that can take one to Broadway?

parts.words: Path that can take one to Broadway?
parts.note: Broadway is a New York street, and the American word for a pavement leads one along it; the surface suggests a career path to theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe a route to stage success, but Broadway is literally a street walked along.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American term for a pavement, the walkway beside a street.

clue.text: Rubbish let off gas

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Junk that releases a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' is idle chatter here, not a vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter idly, as is to gossip or prattle.

clue.text: Patterns on textiles being drawn certainly

parts.note: a drawn game is tied
yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Designs that are definitely being sketched onto fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: These are patterns made by knotting fabric before dyeing, so colour takes unevenly.

clue.text: Old politician, Liberal, in improper diaries

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation sits within the reordered letters
improper means not proper or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A former statesman, a Liberal, revealed in scandalous diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian Conservative Prime Minister, a historic statesman.

clue.text: Old professors turned up one occasion without sign of hesitation

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed letters wrap around the hesitation
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a time is an occasion
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Retired academics showing up one time without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ITIME to EMITI; 'without' puts it around ER: EM-ER-ITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus professors are retired ones keeping their honorary title; this is the plural.

clue.text: Met men cheered in a storm — raising this?

definitions.text: Met men cheered in a storm — raising this?

indicators.note: in a storm means tossed about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Policemen cheering wildly and raising a glass of something green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is London's Metropolitan Police; the whole clue suggests them raising a toast with the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet mint-flavoured liqueur, a drink one might raise in a toast.

clue.text: Boredom shown by English nun confused this writer

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: this writer is the setter speaking, so I

explanation.surface: A writer bored by an English nun's muddled behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless weariness, a French word for tedium.

clue.text: It's inherited from Kelly perhaps

definitions.meaning: a unit of heredity passed from parent to child
... Kelly, the American dancer and film star

explanation.surface: Something passed down from a person named Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of DNA passed down the generations, and also the first name of the dancer Kelly.

clue.text: Something deep in Iowa, old-style country

parts.note: an abyss is a deep chasm
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: Something deep found in Iowa, an old-fashioned land.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, so it is an old name for a nation.

clue.text: Appearance of men on radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Men appearing on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or semblance, the look something takes on.

clue.text: What rough seas do to ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A sailor's description of how a vessel is thrown about in heavy waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one cryptic phrase, but 'to ship' is wordplay: TO taken as written plus SS for a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy waves pitch and throw a boat about violently, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: People out to waylay those not out?

definitions.text: People out to waylay those not out?

parts.words: People out to waylay those not out?
parts.note: strikers who are out stand at the gates to stop colleagues still working; the surface sounds like cricket batsmen not out

explanation.walkthrough: 'out' here means on strike, and 'not out' is a cricket term for batsmen still in, a deliberate distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of strikers stationed outside a workplace to dissuade others from entering is this barrier.
